summary: Oswald Mosley, an aristocratic British MP, turned to fascism after the 1929 crash, founding the British Union of Fascists in 1932, whose Blackshirts waged antisemitic street violence until the Battle of Cable Street and wartime internment.

evidence.note: birth and aristocratic family background begin the biography
elected Conservative MP after the First World War; start of political career
founds the New Party and loses the 1931 election
Rothermere and the Daily Mail promote the BUF and its Blackshirts
Olympia rally: Blackshirts brutally beat anti-fascist hecklers
William Joyce becomes BUF propaganda director and pushes antisemitism
BUF pivots to anti-immigrant, antisemitic appeals to the working class
extended account of the Battle of Cable Street
Blackshirts smash Jewish homes and shops in Stepney after Cable Street
BUF banned and Mosley interned in 1940; postwar Union Movement and death in 1980
Britain First and the Christchurch shooter cited as Mosley's legacy

notes: Postwar career (Union Movement, 1959 campaign) and the Britain First/Christchurch legacy are covered only briefly, so main_span ends at 1940 internment and the 2010s legacy sets reaches_present rather than extending covered_span. NZ is included in setting for the Christchurch segment (title subject) although it is a short coda.
